title: Hybrid multimodal simulation as the ideal architecture for orthopaedic surgical training
description: The article's organizing framework is that an ideal surgical simulator combines physical and virtual elements: physical models provide realistic haptic feedback with real instruments, while computer visualization and AR add objective performance assessment, guidance, visibility of hidden structures, and spatial sound. Citing a literature review, the authors state that "an ideal simulator should be multimodal, combining haptic, visual and audio technology to create an immersive training environment." HipSim instantiates this framework for open surgery, where interaction forces are too large for conventional haptic interfaces.
requirements: Physical components that mimic the mechanical properties of human tissue so trainees can develop force-feedback memory
constraints: Conventional haptic interfaces cannot render the large forces of open surgery tool-bone interaction, so haptic equipment would be limited to reamer-bone interactions while soft-tissue interaction remains physical

target_learning_goals: technical surgical skills rehearsal outside the operating theatre
realistic haptic and perceptual experience of surgery
examples: HipSim pairs a 3D-printed patient-specific pelvis replica with AR anatomy, planning viewfinders, and radiological image navigation on the HoloLens

title: Hypothermia e-learning platform for mountain rescuers with mastery-gated lessons and repeatable tests
description: An e-learning platform developed with the Severe Hypothermia Treatment Centre to train Polish mountain rescue team members in hypothermia recognition and management. It "comprised of a pretest (13 questions), 6 lessons, each followed by a test (4 questions each), and a posttest (13 questions)" covering pathophysiology, post-traumatic hypothermia, avalanches, field management, insulation, and temperature measurement. Learners must score at least 75% on each lesson test to unlock the next lesson, and may repeat lessons, tests, and the post-test. The authors note the curriculum "can easily and periodically be adapted to the current state of knowledge."
requirements: Participants must achieve at least 75% correct (three of four questions) on each lesson test to access the next lesson, repeating the lesson and retest otherwise.
The course was established by professionals experienced in prehospital care and hypothermia treatment and reviewed by the chief physician of the Polish MRT.
constraints: The platform addresses theoretical training; the study did not assess changes in guideline adherence in rescue operations.
target_learners: Professional and volunteer mountain rescuers (qualified first aid providers in Polish mountain rescue teams)
target_learning_goals: Recognition and management of hypothermia in mountain rescue, including post-traumatic hypothermia, field management, insulation, and temperature measurement
examples: 187 rescuers from seven of eight Polish MRTs completed the course between December 2015 and November 2016, with 57 repeating it after 12 months.

title: Hybrid course design allocating factual knowledge to didactic lectures and inquiry topics to 7-jump PBL
description: In this Head and Neck Anatomy course, a 12-week block for first-year dental students, content is split by cognitive demand: "factual knowledge is transferred through didactic lectures, while the topics requiring scientific inquiry are covered through 7-jump PBL methodology". The 7-jump PBL process uses real problems as triggers to motivate learners to take responsibility for their own learning, within a 6-year hybrid dental program combining teacher-centered and student-centered pedagogies.

constraints: The study was conducted in a local academic setting where students had no prior formal education of this type in higher secondary school and met PBL for the first time at undergraduate level.
target_learners: first-year dental undergraduate students in a hybrid dentistry program
target_learning_goals: head and neck anatomy knowledge and its applied aspects
critical thinking and scientific inquiry
examples: The CD-PNU Head and Neck Anatomy course used didactic lectures for topics such as scalp, cranial cavity and brain, and 7-jump PBL for topics such as the parotid gland and facial nerve.
